newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-THIS WEEKEND'S ENGLISH SOCCER LEAGUE MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-THIS WEEKEND'S ENGLISH SOCCER LEAGUE MATCHES.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Aston Villa (6) v Newcastle United (4)
Stunned Newcastle travel to championship rivals Aston Villa, still reeling after the shock resignation of Kevin Keegan, in search of a third consecutive league win.
Villa, with only one defeat in eight league games, are without midfielder Mark Draper (hernia), but recall England defender Gareth Southgate after an ankle injury.

David Ginola should return after a calf injury, but Colombian striker Faustino Asprilla remains sidelined with a hamstring problem. Northern Ireland midfielder Keith Gillespie returns after a bout of influenza.
Blackburn Rovers (17) v Coventry City (12)

Blackburn have taken seven points from their last three games under caretaker-coach Tony Parkes, but they will have to manage without suspended midfielder Billy McKinlay for the next two games. Midfielder Tim Sherwood is hopeful of recovering from a knee injury.

Coventry boast the best recent record in the premier league with four wins and a draw in their last five games. Striker Noel Whelan is out serving a one-match ban while Dion Dublin plays his last game before a three-match suspension.
Leeds United (15) v Leicester City (14)

Leeds, hoping to recover from three straight league defeats, take on an injury-troubled Leicester who are one place above them. Midfielder Lee Sharpe could return for Leeds after a hamstring injury while defenders Gunnar Halle and Carlton Palmer are both banned.

South African defender Lucas Radebe and Ghanian striker Tony Yeboah are both on World Cup duty, but Leeds are boosted by new 1.0 million pounds Dtch defender Robert Molenaar who will make his debut after signing from Volendaam on Thursday.
Liverpool (1) v West Ham United (16)

Leaders Liverpool are hoping to return to winning ways after a shock 2-1 League Cup defeat at struggling Middlesbrough on Wednesday. Former England defender Rob Jones returned in that defeat for the first time since recovering from a fractured vertebra in the FA Cup final against Manchester United last May.
Liverpool have doubts about striker Stan

Collymore (influenza), defender Neil Ruddock (hamstring) and midfielders John Barnes (hamstring) and Jamie Redknapp (ankle). West Ham, only one win in their last five games, hope to recall Australian midfielder Stan Lazaridis after eight weeks out with a groin strain.
Middlesbrough (18) v Southampton (20)

Middlesbrough will be confident of moving away from the relegation zone after their League Cup defeat of Liverpool. Defender Nigel Pearson is out with a neck injury, while Ireland forward Alan Moore and defender Phil Whelan have resumed training after hamstring problems.

Southampton, with only three points from their last six games, are in desperate need of a good result to climb away from the bottom of the table. Coach Graeme Souness is without defenders Richard Dryden (hamstring) and Jason Dodd (knee), while Barry Venison is out with a long-term back problem.
Nottingham Forest (19) v Chelsea (7)
Nottingham Forest, seven points from 12, hope to continue their recent form under player-caretaker coach Stuart Pearce who will keep faith with the team which beat Ipswich 3-0 in the FA Cup.

Chelsea are also in form and looking for a fifth win in six. Norwegian defender Erland Johnsen will come in for Steve Clarke, who is banned for two matches.Gianluca Vialli is still on the sub's bench while fellow-Italian Gianfranco Zola and Welshman Mark Hughes continue in attack.
Sheffield Wednesday (9) v Everton (8)

Sheffield Wednesday are on a 12-game unbeaten streak and will be looking to capitalise on Saturday's 7-1 thrashing of Grimsby in the FA Cup. But Italian striker Benito Carbone (groin) is out for a month and Dutch midfielder Regi Blinker has a sore calf.
Everton will be without midfielder John Ebbrell (ankle operation), midfielders Joe Parkinson and Tony Grant (ankle), but defenders David Unsworth and Terry Phelan return.
Sunderland (11) v Arsenal (2)

A week after drawing at Highbury in the F.A. Cup, the teams meet again. Sunderland have a long injury list and may give a debut to Swedish defender Jan Eriksson, signed from Helsingborgs on Tuesday. Goalkeeper Tony Coton, striker Niall Quinn and defender Lee Howey are out for the season with serious injuries.
Other injury casualties are Martin Scott (groin), Kevin Ball (knee), Paul Stewart (knee), Steve Agnew (wrist) and Martin Smith (back) while midfielder Alex Rae starts a two-match suspension.
Arsenal's England striker Ian Wright is banned and his understudy John Hartson starts a three-match suspension next Wednesday.
Wimbledon (5) v Derby County (13)

Wimbledon, five wins in six and only one defeat in 23 games, remain unexpected title contenders. With no injuries following a 2-0 League Cup win at Bolton on Wednesday, they are at full strength. Striker Dean Holdsworth, has been given compassionate leave to sort out his personal life.
Derby will be without Croatian defender Igor Stimac who underwent a hernia operation on Thursday and is likely to be sidelined for five weeks.
Tottenham Hotspur (10) v Manchester United (3) (Sunday 1600 GMT)

Tottenham will be looking to gain revenge after their 2-0 FA Cup defeat at Manchester United last Sunday. Swiss defender Ramon Vega will be brought into the squad after his 3.7 million pounds arrival from Cagliari on Tuesday, taking Spurs' spending to 10 million pounds in a month.
But Spurs will be without defender John Scales again (hamstring.)

Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson is plagued with defensive worries. International defenders Gary Pallister and Denis Irwin are out through injury with fellow-defender Phil Neville also out from glandular fever. David May may be forced to play through a pain barrier after his hernia operation was postponed.
